verdict.reasoning: Patient reports fever for about seven days and alternating hot/cold with sweating: "I've been struggling with fever for the past week... really hot and sweaty" and "periods of when you're feeling hot and also periods when you're feeling cold as well?" / "Yes".

Patient describes night sweats, muscle aches, nausea with reduced intake, and fatigue: "I'm really hot and sweaty all the time", "I'm aching all over", "I'm feeling quite nauseous, so I've not been able to eat very much... Just generally quite tired and unwell. I'm sweating during the night." Constant elevated temperature is reasonably inferred from persistent fever and symptoms.

Patient states: "I've been trying to like take ibuprofen and paracetamol... but it's not really helping. Just been taking the recommended dose every day of those" and then clarifies partial relief: "Perhaps slightly, yes, but I'm still experiencing these symptoms, so it does take the edge off of it."

Cough/sore throat/ear pain: "Have you got any cough or cold or sore throat...?" / "Not those sort of symptoms"; "Have you had an ear pain at all?" / "No". Diarrhea: "Have you had any diarrhea?" / "Not really, no". Neck stiffness: "Have you got any neck stiffness at all?" / "No". Dysuria/frequency: "Any problems... when you're passing urine?" / "No" and "Any painful urination at all?" / "Not at all, no"; "Are you passing urine more often than normal?" / "I don't think so". Rash: "have you got any rash... ?" / "I haven't noticed any rashes". Joint swelling aside from back pain: "Any joints swollen or tender or sore?" / "Not really. I mean, I often have problems with back pain".

Travel to Vietnam and mixed rural/urban trekking and cycling are supported, but river/beach exposure is not: doctor asks about rivers/beaches, and the patient only confirms trekking and cycling through farmland: "Were you going out into the rivers? Were you going on beaches?" / patient responds only with "we were sort of trekking and cycling through farmland" with no mention of rivers or beaches.

Patient states: "I did" take malaria preventative medication, thinks it was daily, and mentions a second pill without recalling names: "I think it was daily" and "I think it was another one that I took on top of the first one" and "I can't remember now off the top of my head."

Chronic mechanical back pain is described: "I often have problems with back pain" and physio attributes it to posture and prolonged sitting: "They've said that it's related to long periods of time sitting at a desk and just bad posture."
Patient describes episodic migraines and headaches: "Sometimes I struggle with migraines and headaches."
Pollen allergy/hay fever: "No, I'm just really. Pollen allergy, that's all I have." and doctor clarifies: "Okay, so hay fever?" / "Yes. Yeah, just hay fever."

Acute use of paracetamol: same quote as above: "I've been trying to like take ibuprofen and paracetamol... Just been taking the recommended dose every day of those."

Family history: "The main one would be heart attack. My. My father passed away of that." and "How old is he when that happens?" / "68, I think." Myocardial infarction is equivalent to heart attack.
"What do you work as?" / "I work as a nurse."
"And are you a smoker at all?" / "No, I'm not."
"And do you drink much alcohol?" / "Moderate alcohol intake? Drink too much." (Implying moderate drinking.)

"And you're up to date with all the vaccinations, Hepatitis B, that kind of thing?" / "Yes, indeed. Yeah."

Consultation appears entirely by phone/video, and no vitals or physical exam are mentioned. The doctor explicitly plans an in-person exam later: "we're going to need to bring you into one of our clinics exam" indicating none done yet.

Clinician links febrile illness with recent Vietnam travel and plans malaria/tropical infection workup: "we need to find a reason for why you've got this fever" and "you've recently come from Vietnam... we need to think about things like malaria or other exotic infections as well... I'll be asking for something called thick and thin blood films to check for malaria and inflammatory markers and things like that."
Chronic low back pain discussed as mechanical/postural: "I often have problems with back pain" and physio diagnosis: "related to long periods of time sitting at a desk and just bad posture."
Episodic headaches/migraines noted: "Sometimes I struggle with migraines and headaches."

Same-day (immediate) in-clinic exam in central London offered and accepted: "we're going to need to bring you into one of our clinics exam" and "You can come into one of our clinics in central London. That's one option" and patient: "I can come straight into central London today to get that sorted."

The doctor only specifies "thick and thin blood films to check for malaria and inflammatory markers and things like that." CBC, U&E, LFTs, CRP/ESR, and "other tropical serology" are not explicitly mentioned.

Alternative of A&E and implied urgency given: "if it's inconvenient for you to come into central London... you could actually just attend a local ae". While deterioration wording is not explicit, A&E is advised if clinic not feasible.

Doctor does advise staying off work: "I don't think you can go into work until we've sorted this out." Hydration and continued paracetamol/ibuprofen are not advised in the plan; these medications and drinking are only described in history, with no explicit recommendation to continue or to hydrate.

Back pain management (physiotherapy and posture/strength exercises) is described as current practice, but no explicit plan or advice is given during this consultation to continue it: "I'm under a physiotherapist at the moment for that... exercises are focused on improving posture and strength."

Clinician will document plan and asks patient to call admin: "I'm going to type up what my thought process is and what kind of tests I think you need in the notes for this appointment" and "I will send a message to one of our admin team members asking them to book you in, and if you can, ring the number that I leave in your consultation notes after a few minutes and then they'll slot you in."
